title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
tagline: The whole book, chapter by chapter, with one reader’s marginalia.
coverIntro: Below is the voyage entire — every chapter a landing on the trail, colored by its waters. The faint arcs are the places my notes reach across the book: hover a chapter to see what it speaks to and what speaks back. Click one and start reading; sentences underlined in red carry my notes, and each chapter ends with what I make of it.
about: Melville calls the world a loom — “the weaver-god, he weaves” — and this page is my attempt to weave a second thread through his. What you are reading is the Project Gutenberg text of Moby-Dick (the 1851 American edition), unaltered, split into its {sections} sections. Alongside it I have written {essays} chapter readings and pinned {notes} notes to particular sentences.

A word on what the notes are. They are not a study guide. They are the places where, reading as carefully as I can, I stopped — because a sentence turned on itself, or told a joke nobody laughs at, or said the thing the rest of the book is circling. Where I am unsure I say so. Where I disagree with the usual reading I say that too. You should treat them as a reading companion who talks a bit too much and can be ignored by not clicking.

Some practical things. Your place is remembered in this browser only. The chart on the left divides the book into four waters, which is my division, not Melville’s; the search box finds phrases anywhere in the text. On a wide screen the notes sit in the margin; on a narrow one they open when you click the underlined line. ← and → turn chapters.

And a suggestion: read the Extracts. Everyone skips them. They are Melville clearing his throat for eighty quotations and they tell you exactly what kind of book this is going to be — one that would rather include everything than choose.

movements.name: Ashore
movements.desc: New Bedford and Nantucket. Ishmael finds a bedfellow, a sermon, a ship, and a prophet; the sea is still a promise.

movements.name: The Ship
movements.desc: The Pequod at sea. The crew, the mates, Ahab at last, the doubloon nailed to the mast, and the whiteness of the whale.

movements.name: The Hunt
movements.desc: Lowering, killing, cutting-in, trying-out; other ships met; whole chapters given to the whale’s head, tail, skin, and skeleton.

movements.name: The Chase
movements.desc: The Pacific. The coffin, the forge, the candles, the Rachel, one quiet morning — and three days.
